output.summary:
I'd keep 14 of the 16 Deafened tests. Every green test failed under at least one targeted mutation. Two of my mutations had no effect at first, and both turned out to be my mistakes, not weak tests. Treating Deafened as Blinded in game.can_see doesn't reach the check, which goes through Condition.d20. Adding `or "hearing" in tags` at creature.py:456 doesn't fail anything, because the auto path still rolls when acc.auto is None. Better mutations (Deafened auto-fails every check; acc.fail on any hearing-tagged check) made those tests fail.

The red test, test_deafened_automatic_failure_cites_the_rule, fails for the reason its xfail marker gives. Creature.check passes page '6' and no rule, so d20.py:163 logs the auto-fail under the generic check rule instead of GLOSS.deafened#2 on p.181.

I refuted two tests at confidence 0.4, so they go to a person: test_deafened_perception_by_sight_is_rolled and test_deafened_check_command_rolls_an_ordinary_perception_check. Both expect an untagged Perception check by a Deafened creature to be rolled. That is stage-A's Reading A, proposed at confidence 0.6, and the README register has no ruling on it. Under Reading B the expected result flips. The second test also largely duplicates the first, only going through the Session command.

The scenario test test_cond03 (tests/scenarios/test_damage_rest.py) overlaps partly with the basic auto-fail test and the Athletics test. The SRD tests make more assertions, so I don't count them as duplicates.
